craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of workshop disputation — ends-first reasoning. Both extremes fenced (no-Lord-no-un-Lord); atomic-mark refused. Rejected: (a) picking a horn → killed: fencing is the verse. Read aloud: HE-stands-PROVED NOT by-POT-ness … TAKES the-A-tom-ic-MARK in-DEED.

lines: He stands proved not by pot-ness but by answered need;
no Lord, no un-Lord takes the atomic mark indeed.
l4.sanskrit_cite: na ghaṭāditayā siddhaḥ so'rthitāparipūrakaḥ na ceśvaro'nīśvaro vā prakṛto'trāṇulakṣaṇaḥ

reads_against.argmap: Lord or non-Lord? → Both extremes fenced: neither Lord nor un-Lord atomically taken.
c1_essence: Potter necessary, nature watching, helpers insufficient, wisdom and will required, sufficiency tested (vv28-33).
Array excels by ends; Lord and un-Lord fenced off atomically; pradhāna will-less yet person-aim-ness stands (vv34-36).
